info.title: SENAITE JSON API
info.description: The JSON REST API of SENAITE LIMS, an open-source laboratory information management system built on Plone. It is provided by the `senaite.jsonapi` add-on, which mounts itself at the Plone site's `@@API` traversal point with the base route `/senaite/v1`; a full URL therefore looks like `https://<host>/<plone-site>/@@API/senaite/v1/<route>`. Every SENAITE portal type is reachable through one generic content route — reads by GET, and create / update / delete by POST with the operation in the path — plus dedicated routes for users, authentication, catalogs, registry, settings, search and push. The OpenFn `senaite` adaptor exposes a single generic `request(method, path, options)` operation against this base, logging in first with `GET /login?__ac_name=&__ac_password=` and reusing the session cookie.

servers.description: The public SENAITE demo instance. A real deployment is `https://<host>/<plone-site>/@@API/senaite/v1`, e.g. `https://lims.example.org/senaite/@@API/senaite/v1`.

get.summary: Get the API version at the base URL
get.description: The JSON API base route (`@@API/senaite/v1`) answers with the same payload as `/version`.

Returns an empty object for an authenticated caller. For an anonymous caller it answers 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate: basic realm="JSONAPI AUTH"` header, which makes a browser show the Basic login prompt.

SENAITE indexes content in several catalogs. This route reports each catalog with the indexes that can be used as search filters and sort keys, the metadata schema it stores, and the portal types it holds.
Returns the catalog record directly (not wrapped in the batch envelope).

parameters.name: catalog_id
parameters.description: Catalog id, e.g. `portal_catalog`, `senaite_catalog_sample`, `bika_catalog`.

post.description: Creates an object. The portal type comes from the `<resource>` path segment or from `portal_type` in the body; the target container comes from the `<uid>` path segment or from `parent_path` / `parent_uid` in the body. Creation into the portal root or into `senaite/bika_setup` is refused with 401. Everything is taken from the request body on this form of the route.

get.summary: Log in and issue a JWT (deprecated GET form)
get.description: Authenticates the caller and issues a JSON Web Token. Two modes are supported: HTTP Basic auth (no body fields needed), or a form login with `__ac_name` / `__ac_password`. The response body is the `/users/<userid>` payload with `token` and `expires` merged in; the token is also set as the HttpOnly `token` cookie, and the Plone session cookie `__ac` is set. Subsequent calls authenticate with either the cookie or `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The JWT half of this arrived in senaite.jsonapi 2.7.0 and needs its GenericSetup profile installed; on 2.6.x and earlier the route sets only the `__ac` session cookie and returns no `token`.

parameters.name: __ac_name
parameters.description: User name (form login).

parameters.name: __ac_password
parameters.description: Password (form login). Passing credentials on a GET is deprecated in senaite.jsonapi and is scheduled for removal in 2.8.0 — use POST.

200.description: The authenticated user plus the issued JWT.

get.description: Searches across content without naming a portal type. Any index of the queried catalog may be passed as an extra query parameter (`portal_type`, `id`, `review_state`, `getClientID`, ...); `catalog` selects which catalog to query, since SENAITE spreads content over several. Results are batched and, per the API's two-step design, carry only catalog metadata unless `complete=yes` is set.

get.summary: List content of one portal type
get.description: senaite.jsonapi exposes every SENAITE portal type through one generic content route. Reads are HTTP GET; create, update and delete are HTTP POST, with the operation named in the path (`<resource>/create`, `create/<uid>`, ...). `delete` deactivates the object rather than removing it, because SENAITE keeps a full audit trail. Any catalog index may be used as a query parameter. Passing a 32-character UID in place of the portal type returns that one record on its own — the bare content object, not the batch envelope.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: A SENAITE portal type, e.g. `Client`, `Contact`, `AnalysisRequest`, `AnalysisService`. Lower-case spellings are accepted. A 32-character UID may be given instead, in which case the single record with that UID is returned.

post.summary: Run create/update/delete on one object via a method override
post.description: POST to an object without naming the operation in the path. The operation is taken from the `X-HTTP-Method-Override` header (`create`, `update` or `delete`), which is how Backbone.js-style clients drive the API.

basicAuth.description: HTTP Basic auth with a SENAITE user name and password.

bearerAuth.description: The JSON Web Token returned by `/login`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

sessionCookie.name: __ac
sessionCookie.description: The Plone session cookie set by `/login`. This is what the OpenFn senaite adaptor reuses.

tokenCookie.name: token
tokenCookie.description: HttpOnly cookie carrying the same JWT that `/login` returns in the body.

b_start.name: b_start
b_start.description: Index of the first item of the requested batch page.

catalog.name: catalog
catalog.description: Catalog to search against, e.g. `senaite_catalog_sample`. Defaults to `portal_catalog`.

children.name: children
children.description: Include a folder's contents under the `children` key. Only honoured with `complete` or a UID.

complete.name: complete
complete.description: Return the full object data immediately instead of only catalog metadata (bypasses the two-step design).

created_since.name: created_since
created_since.description: Items created since a date (`%Y-%m-%d`, `%Y%m%d%H%M%S`, or a relative `2d` / `2h`).

filedata.name: filedata
filedata.description: Include file fields as base64 data.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Page size; the response is batched into pages of this many items.

modified_since.name: modified_since
modified_since.description: Items modified since a date (`%Y-%m-%d`, `%Y%m%d%H%M%S`, or a relative `2d` / `2h`).

path.name: path
path.description: Physical path; only results below it are returned.

recent_created.name: recent_created
recent_created.description: Items created within this range up to today.

recent_modified.name: recent_modified
recent_modified.description: Items modified within this range up to today.

sort_limit.name: sort_limit
sort_limit.description: Limit the result set the catalog returns to n items.

workflow.name: workflow
workflow.description: Include workflow data under the `workflow` key.

Unauthorized.description: The caller is anonymous or lacks the permission the route requires.

NotFound.description: No such route, portal type or object.

AnalysisRequest.description: A sample (portal type `AnalysisRequest` — in SENAITE the sample is modelled as an analysis request).

Catalog.description: A catalog registered in the SENAITE instance, with the indexes that can be used as search filters or sort keys, the metadata schema it stores, and the portal types it indexes.

count.description: Number of items found — can exceed the page size.

page.description: Current page of the batched result set.

_runtime.description: Time the server needed to build the payload.

next.description: URL of the next page, or null.

previous.description: URL of the previous page, or null.

ContentActionRequest.description: Body of a create / update / delete action. Every field of the target portal type may be sent alongside the addressing fields below.

portal_type.description: Type to create. Required on `create` when the path does not name the resource.

parent_path.description: Physical path of the target container, e.g. `/senaite/clients`.

parent_uid.description: UID of the target container, instead of `parent_path`.

uid.description: UID of the object to update or deactivate.

path.description: Physical path of the object to update or deactivate.

transition.description: Workflow transition to run after an update, e.g. `receive`, `publish`.

ContentActionResponse.description: Response of a create / update / delete action: the records the action affected.

url.description: URL of the action route that ran.

ContentList.description: Batched list of content records — the standard response envelope of every list, search and read route.

ContentRecord.description: One SENAITE content object as the JSON API returns it. In a list or search response this is the catalog metadata for the object; with `complete=yes`, or when the object is addressed by UID, it is the full field set. The fields below are the ones every record carries — every other key is the catalog index or schema field of that portal type.

id.description: Object id within its container, e.g. `WB-00012`.

url.description: Object URL in the SENAITE UI.

api_url.description: Object URL in this JSON API.

Error.description: Error payload. `type` carries the senaite.jsonapi exception class name (`BadRequestError`, `UnauthorizedError`, `NotFoundError`, ...).

LoginRequest.description: Form login credentials. Omit both fields when authenticating with HTTP Basic.

LoginResponse.description: The `/users/<userid>` payload for the authenticated caller, with the issued JWT merged in.

count.description: Number of items found — can exceed the page size.

page.description: Current page of the batched result set.

_runtime.description: Time the server needed to build the payload.

next.description: URL of the next page, or null.

previous.description: URL of the previous page, or null.

token.description: Signed JSON Web Token; also set as the HttpOnly `token` cookie.

expires.description: Unix timestamp at which the token expires.

PushRequest.description: One record for a named push consumer. Every field other than `consumer` is passed through to the consumer adapter.

success.description: Whether the consumer processed the record.

page.description: Current page of the batched result set.

_runtime.description: Time the server needed to build the payload.

next.description: URL of the next page, or null.

previous.description: URL of the previous page, or null.
